newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Japanese emperor begins two-day visit to Argentina.
newsitem.headline: Japanese emperor begins two-day visit to Argentina.

text.p: Japan's Emperor Akihito and Empress Michiko began a two-day visit to the Argentine capital on Monday, their last stop on the first Japanese imperial visit to Latin America.

The couple arrived from a 10-day visit to Brazil, home to the largest Japanese community abroad and the only other country they visited. They were greeted by a large delegation headed by Foreign Minister Guido di Tella.

Official activities start on Tuesday when they will attend a reception at the presidential residence and meet privately with President Carlos Menem. Dinner will be hosted by Menem at an elegant downtown hotel, the Alvear Palace.

Akihito and Michiko, who leave for Japan on Wednesday morning, have been protected throughout their trip by Japanese police rather than the imperial guards normally used on foreign visits. The change was attributed to growing security concerns after the fourth-month hostage crisis at the Japanese ambassador's home in Lima.

The imperial couple began their visit to Latin America on May 31 in Belem, a Brazilian port at the mouth of the Amazon river. Later they travelled to Brasilia to meet President Fernando Henrique Cardoso and thrilled fans in Sao Paulo, home to most of the 1.3 million Brazilians of Japanese descent.
